title: introduce-soft-schema-affinity-and-fragment-repair-for-openai-tool-calls
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: production LLM streams occasionally deliver partial or fragmented tool schema information which causes incorrect tool_choice decisions, duplicate tool invocations, or hard failures when the compatibility adapter expects an exact schema match. This PR implements a soft-schema affinity layer that assigns confidence scores to candidate tools based on partial schema intersection, argument name proximity, prior message context (prefix/KV cache signals), and streaming continuity heuristics; it also adds a fragment-repair handler that coalesces broken JSON or framed tool-invoke payloads across stream chunks into a normalized invoke envelope. The OpenAI compatibility adapter is updated to prefer soft-bound tool variants when confidence exceeds a configurable threshold and to fall back to the existing deterministic router for exact matches. A route-level feature flag "soft_bind" (default: false) allows staged rollout for Dedicated/Private customers. Changes include: server/openai_compat/soft_schema_bind.py: affinity matcher and scoring; server/streaming/recovery_handler.rs: fragment coalescer and continuity token heuristics; sdk/python/redwood/openai_compat.py: opt-in soft_bind per-route and telemetry hooks; docs/openai-tooling.md: migration and behavior notes; tests/integration/test_toolcall_fallback.py: cross-chunk fragment tests; ci/pipelines/compat.yml: rerun-on-flaky integration tolerance. Checklist: [x] design doc linked to Linear ENG-4321; [x] unit tests; [x] integration tests covering cross-chunk fragments; [x] perf benchmarks (p99 within target); [x] docs and migration notes; [x] feature flag gating for gradual rollout. Migration notes: default behavior remains unchanged; enable soft_bind to reduce false-negative tool routing and to decrease spurious tool errors observed in streaming scenarios. Backwards compatibility: preserved; no public API schema changes. Performance: microbenchmarks show ~1.8% median latency regression under synthetic high-fragmentation load while reducing fallback tool invocations by ~12%. Risk: low-to-moderate due to concurrency in the recovery handler; addressed with stress tests and a short TTL on repair buffers. Related work and references: ENG-4321, PM-118, SUP-9988 (customer report).

release_notes: Add opt-in 'soft_bind' mode for OpenAI-compatible tool calls that improves robustness to fragmented or partial schema payloads by scoring candidates and repairing stream fragments; enabled via route config; default off.
